question: Ravikirti was the court poet of which ruler?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakeshin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ravikirti was the court poet of **Pulakeshin II**, a prominent ruler of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
• He is best known for composing the **Aihole inscription**, which details the achievements of Pulakeshin II.
 
• The Aihole inscription, written in Sanskrit, is inscribed at the Meguti Jain temple in Aihole, Karnataka.
 
• Ravikirti's inscription describes Pulakeshin II's military conquests, including his victory over Harshavardhana and his expansion of the Chalukya empire.
 
• This inscription is considered an important historical source for understanding the Chalukya dynasty and its socio-political context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulakeshin II (610–642 CE):**

 
 
• Pulakeshin II was one of the greatest rulers of the Chalukya dynasty and ruled from Badami in present-day Karnataka.
 
• He successfully resisted the northward expansion of Harshavardhana, as documented in Ravikirti's Aihole inscription.
 
• Under his reign, the Chalukya empire expanded to include large parts of the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Aihole:**
 
 
• Aihole is an important historical site known as the "Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture."
 
• It was a major cultural and architectural center during the Chalukya period.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Chalukyas were a prominent South Indian dynasty that ruled from the 6th to the 12th century CE.
 
• They are known for their contributions to art, architecture, and literature, as seen in their temple constructions and inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Court Poets:**
 
 
• Court poets like Ravikirti played a crucial role in documenting the achievements of their patrons.
 
• Such inscriptions often combined historical records with poetic flourishes, serving as both propaganda and cultural artifacts.
